context:
Goal: builders never write test content (your item 437 a).
Problem (rule): mutants are broken copies of guard code that prove a test catches the fault. They live in hooks/mutate_guard.py, hooks/mutate_shared.py and janitor/mutate_sweep.py. Main lets a builder write them (decisions agents-get-standing-rules and red-run-trailer-on-test-commits; the coordinator's pick c, Nov 7). Item 437 a ruled on test files and does not name mutants, so whether it covers them needs your word.
Based on (read): #2310's builder wrote six mutants, and the builder guard let them through by design (AUTHOR_MUTATION_TESTS in hooks/guard.py).
Departs from: main lets builders add mutants — option a makes them test-author only.
Meanwhile: step builder-edits-mutation-tests waits. #1675 is held with runner 8, because its decision text says builders may add mutants. #1904 merges as it is, because its text does not name mutants.

options.gain: The builder never grades its own code.
options.label: Mutants are test content: only a test-author writes them
options.lose: One more hand-off in each guard lane.

options.label: Keep the builder carve-out
options.lose: A builder can write mutants that its own code is sure to kill.

ref: step builder-edits-mutation-tests; PR #2310 (the incident); PR #1675 (held); your item 437 a
reply: Routed 17:24 CST Nov 8: mutants are test content, test-author only. Home: step builder-edits-mutation-tests (roadmap 3040349f3); the coordinator routes it, and #1675's text gets the same rewrite.
title: Are mutants test content, so only a test-author writes them and a builder never does?
